commentary.headline: Cheap for a reason — I would keep looking.
body: Nissan Micra at $12,995. The price looks tempting, but this is a model I would steer her away from.
It shows 92,602 km.
Realistically about $15,589 to get it on the road — roughly $2,594 on top of the asking price. I have allowed for pre-purchase inspection and winter tires. Insurance is not in that figure.

Nissan's continuously variable transmissions from this era fail often, frequently between 120,000 and 180,000 km. A replacement runs $4,000-$6,000 installed. The cars are cheap on the used market for exactly this reason. If one is irresistible, insist on documented CVT replacement or fluid-service history.
